हिरण्यपुर: Hiraṇyapura1 nt.: The city of the Nivātakavaca demons. A. Location: In the bay of the ocean (निवातकवचा नाम दानवा … । समुद्र-कुक्षिम् आश्रित्य दुर्गे प्रतिवसन्त्य् उत) 3. 165. 10: at the end of the ocean (पारे समुद्रस्य) 4. 56. 11; 5. 48. 16; one had to cross the ocean to reach it (अपश्यम् उदधिम्) 3. 166. 1; (तम् अतीत्य … सर्वाम्-भोनिधिं … अपश्यं … तद् दैत्यपुरम् अन्तिकात्) 3. 166. 6; also said to be located in the Pātāla (पातालतलम् आश्रितम्) 5. 98. 2. B. Creation: Conceived mentally and created with great effort by the architect Maya in Pātāla (हिरण्यपुरम् एतत् … अनल्-पेन प्रयत्नेन निर्मितं विश्वकर्मणा । मयेन मनसा सृष्टम् पातालतलम् आश्रि-तम्) 5. 98. 1-2. C. Description: City of Daityas (दैत्यपुर) 3. 166. 6); full of Dānavas (दानवाकीर्ण) 3. 166. 6; residence of Dānavas (दानवालय) 3. 165. 23; city of Daityas and Dānavas (दैत्यानां दानवा-नां च) 5. 98. 1; city of the Asuras (पुरम् आसुरम्) 3. 166. 11; famous (ख्यात) 5. 98. 1; best (उत्तम) 3. 169. 26; excellent town (पुरवर) 5. 98. 1; having a wonderful shape (अद्भुताकार) 3. 169. 26; big (म-हन्त्) 5. 98. 1; inaccessible (दुर्ग) 3. 165. 10; very formidable (अत्युग्र) 3. 165. 23; excelling the city of gods (विशिष्तं देव-नगरात्) 3. 169. 26; excelling the city of Pura-ndara (Indra) (पुरन्दरपुरात् … विशिष्तम्) 3. 169. 27; the houses of the Nivātakavacas were made of gold, beset with gems (वेश्मा-नि … बहुरत्नविचित्राणि शातकुम्भमयानि च) 3. 169. 25; the golden and silvery houses of Hiraṇyapura, the houses shining like the sun (वेश्मानि रौक्माणि … राजतानि च … सूर्यरूपाणि चाभान्ति) described in some details 5. 98. 9-12; it was impossible to describe their appearance and the materials used for their construction; they were perfected in qualities; (hence) they had proper form and qualities (नैतानि शक्यं निर्देष्टुं रूपतो द्रव्यतस् तथा । गुणतश् चैव सिद्धानि प्रमाणगुणवन्ति च ॥ ) 5. 98. 13; there were places of amusement and the houses were provided with jewelled beds and precious vessels and seats (आक्रीडान् पश्य दैत्यानां तथैव शयनान्य् उत । रत्न-वन्ति महार्हाणि भाजनान्य् आसनानि च ॥ ) 5. 98. 14 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 100. 14: आक्री-डान् क्रीडास्थानानि); there were mountains, looking like clouds and full of streams, and trees giving flowers and fruits accord-ing to one's desire and moving at will (जल-दाभांस् तथा शैलांस् तोयप्रस्रवणान्वि-तान् । कामपुष्पफलांश् चैव पादपान् कामचारिणः ॥ ) 5. 98. 15; it was called पुर 3. 166. 6, 7, 10, 11; 3. 169. 3, 22, 28; 5. 98. 1; नगर 3. 169. 21, 26, 35. D. History: As told by Mātali to Arjuna: The city once belonged to the king of gods (Indra); the Nivātakavaca demons practised severe austerities, satisfied Pitāmaha (Brahma-deva) and obtained as a boon this city for their residence and for freedom from fear of gods in battles (इदं वृतं निवासाय देवेभ्यश् चाभयं युधि ॥ ); Indra, out of self-interest, agreed to what the demons had asked for (विधत्तां भगवान् अत्रेत्य् आत्मनो हितकाम्यया); the Nivātakavacas then drove out gods from this place and made the city their residence (ततो निवात-कवचैर् इतः प्रच्याविताः सुराः) 3. 169. 28-30); (निवातकवचा नाम दानवाः … प्रती-वसन्त्य् उत) 3. 165. 10; 1. 2. 121; 5. 166. 34 (?). E. Epic event: Arjuna, at the instance of Indra, attacked the residence of Dānavas riding the chariot driven by Mātali (तांस् तत्र जहि कौन्तेय … ततो मातलिसं युक्तंप्रादान् मे रथम्) 3. 165. 10-12; (दानवालयम् अत्युग्रं प्रयातो ऽस्मि) 3. 165. 23; battle described in 3. 166. 7-23; 3. 167-3-169. 20; when the Nivātaka-vacas were killed, their wives cried aloud in the city (दारास् तेषां तु सर्वशः । प्राक्रो-शन् नगरे तस्मिन्) 3. 168. 21; Arjuna entered the town along with Mātali frighten-ing the women by the loud sound of the chariot; after killing Nivātakavacas, Arjuna returned to the residence of the gods (ततो मातलिना सार्धम् अहं तत् पुरम् अभ्य-याम्) 3. 169. 22; (पुनर् मातलिना सार्धम् अगच्छं देवसद्म तत्) 3. 169. 35; (निहत्य … निवातकवचांश् चैव ततो ऽहं शक्रम् आगमम्) 3. 170. 61; Mātali told Indra the killing of Nivātakavacas 3. 170. 63; according to Indra, Arjuna's feat excell-ed that of gods and Asuras (अतिदेवासुरं कर्म कृतम् एतद् त्वया रणे) 3. 170. 66; the incident is referred to on several occa-sions: (1) In the list of the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan in the Parvasaṃgrahapar-van (निवातकवचैर् युद्धं हिरण्यपुर-वासिभिः) 1. 2. 121; (2) By Arjuna while describing his feats to Uttara (अहं पारे समुद्रस्य हिरण्यपुरम् आरुजम्) 4. 56. 11; (3) By Bhīṣma while addressīng Duryodhana (एष पारे समुद्रस्य हिरण्य-पुरम् आरुजत् । हत्वा षष्टिसहस्राणि निवात-कवचान् रणे) 5. 48. 16; (4) By Bhīṣma again while giving his estimate to Duryodha-na about the heroes assembled on the side of the Pāṇḍavas (दानवानां सहस्राणि हिर-ण्यपुरवासिनाम् । हतान्य् एकरथेनाजौ) 5. 166. 34 (but this could also refer to the killing of Paulomas and Kālakeyas of Hiraṇya-pura2); (5) By Yudhiṣṭhira when he, while lamenting over the death of Abhi-manyu, referred to Arjuna's exploits (निवा-तकवचाञ् जघ्ने कालकेयांश् च … । हिरण्य-पुरवासिनः) 7. 49. 16-17 (Kālakeyas seem here to be identified with Kālakhañjas who, with Nivātakavacas, lived in Hiraṇyapura1 5. 98. 5, 7); (6) By Jayadratha, frightened by the vow of Arjuna (दानवानां सह-स्राणि हिरण्यपुरवासिनाम् । जघान … देव-राजप्रचोदितः) 7. 53. 22; (7) By Droṇa, while reminding Duryodhana of Arjuna's past exploits (निवातकवचाश् चापि … तेन वीरेण निर्जिताः) 7. 160. 18; दानवानां सह-स्राणि हिरण्यपुर्वासिनाम् । विजिग्ये पुरुष-व्याघ्रः) 7. 160. 19 (but this could also refer to the killing of Paulomas and Kāla-keyas in addition to the Nivātakavacas of st. 18). F. Past event: While telling Mātali about Hiraṇypura, Nārada mentions the defeat of Indra several times at the hands of the Nivātakavacas of Hiraṇya-pura 5. 98. 7-8.

Hiraṇyapura2 nt.: Name of the town of the demons called Kālakeyas (or Kāla-khañjas) and Paulomas. A. History: As told by Mātali to Arjuna: A Daiteyī named Pulomā and a Mahāsurī named Kālakā practised severe austerities for one thousand divine years of gods; at the end of their austerities they received a boon by which they secured less misery for their sons and impossibility of being killed by gods, demons and ser-pents: they also received the city Hiraṇya-pura, made for the Kālakeyas by Brah-man and occupied by the demons, the sons of Pulomā and Kālakā (अगृह्णीतां वरं ते तु सुतानाम् अल्पदुःखताम् । अव-ध्यतां च … राजेन्द्र पन्नगासुरराक्ष-सैः … ॥ … पुरं चेदं … ब्रह्मणा … कालकेयकृते कृतम् … पौलोमाध्युषितं … कालकेयैश् च दानवैः ॥ हिरण्यपुरम् इत्य् एतत् ख्यायते नगरम्) 3. 170. 6-11; पौ-लोमैः कालकेयैश् च … अधिष्ठितम्) 3. 170. 2; (रक्षितं कालकेयैश् च पौलोमैश् च महासुरैः) 3. 170. 11; (त एते … अव-ध्याः सर्वदैवतैः । निवसन्त्य् अत्र 3. 170. 12; hence called city of demons (दानव-पुर) 3. 170. 58: (दैत्यानां पुरम्) 3. 170. 5; city where demons lived happily due to a boon (दैतेयैर् वरदानेन धार्-यते स्म यथासुखम्) 3. 170. 23; full of Asuras everywhere (असुरैः … सर्वतो वृतम्) 3. 170. 4. B. Description: Heavenly (दिव्य) 3. 170. 1, 3. 10. 23; of heavenly lustre (दिव्यवर्चस्) 3. 170. 23; having the lustre of fire and sun (पावकार्कसमप्र-भ) 3. 170. 1; beset with jewels all around (सर्वरत्नमय) 3. 170. 3; (सर्वरत्नैः समुदितम्) 3. 170. 8; of well-executed lustre (सुकृतप्रभ) 3. 170. 8; like Amarā-vatī (अमरावतिसंकाश) 3. 170. 25; of the form of the city of Gandharvas (गन्धर्-वनगराकार) 3. 170. 59; of wonderful sight (अद्भुतदर्शन) 3. 170. 5; (अद्भु-तोपमदर्शन) 3. 170. 3; big (महन्त्) 3. 170. 11, 54; moving in the sky (खग) 3. 170. 54; (खचर) 3. 170. 8. 10, 23; moving as desired (कामग) 3. 170. 23; (कामगम) 3. 170. 25; (कामचर) 3. 170. 1; endowed with all desires and qualities (सर्वकामगुणोपेत) 3. 170. 9; healthy (अनामय) 3. 170. 9; free from sorrow (वीतशोक) 3. 170. 9; having gates and watchtowers (गोपुराट्टालकोपेत) and four gates (चतुर्द्वार) 3. 170. 3; full of trees which were beset with jewels, were bright and full of flowers and fruits (द्रुमै रत्नमयैश् चित्रैः … अधि-ष्ठितम्) 3. 170. 2; (द्रुमैः पुष्पफलोपे-तैर् दिव्यरत्नमयैर् वृतम्) 3. 170. 3; full of bright, heavenly and very attractive birds (भास्वरैश् च पतत्रिभिः … अधिष्ठि-तम्) 3. 170. 2; (पतत्रिभिर् दिव्यैर् उपेतं सुमनोहरैः) 3. 170. 4; inaccessible (दुरा-सद) 3. 170. 3; difficult to be attacked even by gods together with Yakṣas and Gandharvas (दुर्धर्षम् अमरैर् अपि । स-यक्षगन्धर्वगणैः) 3. 170. 8; as also by serpents, Asuras and Rākṣasas (पन्नगा-सुरराक्षसैः) 3. 170. 8; hence avoided by gods (अमरवर्जित) 3. 170. 10; but after the demons were killed by Arjuna, the city, whose rulers were killed, lacked all lustre, became devoid of glory, was full of grief, and was struck by sorrow and miserable condition; it then did not shine as before (तच् छोकयुक्तम् अश्रीकं दुःखदैन्य-समाहतम् । न बभौ दानवपुरं हत-त्विट्कं हतेश्वरम् ॥ ) 3. 170. 58; usually referred to as पुर (cf. the name Hiraṇya-pura) 3. 170. 1, 5, 8, 13, 21, 23, 25, 26, 54, 55, 58, 59, but also as नगर 3. 170. 11, 21, 55. C. Characteristic: As the city could move at will (see above B. Description: (कामग, कामगम); it could go underground and again rise high above, and then again moving quickly and obliquely submerge in waters (अन्तर् भू-मौ निपतितं पुनर् ऊर्ध्वं प्रतिष्ठते । पुनस् तिर्यक् प्रयात्य् आशु पुनर् अप्सु निम-ज्जति ॥ ) 3. 170. 24. D. Epic event: Arjuna, while returning to the residence of gods after killing the Nivātakavaca demons, saw on way the town Hiraṇyapura 3. 170. 1; on hearing from Mātali about the de-mons occupying the town (3. 170. 8-10), Arjuna asked Mātali to take him to Hiraṇyapura so that he might kill the demons; accordingly Mātali drove him there quickly in the heavenly chariot 3. 170. 13-15; the battle between Arjuna and the demons in the town described (3. 170. 16-50); when the demons were being killed they employed माया of the demons and flew up in the sky together with the town (ते वध्यमाना दैतेयाः पुरम् आस्थाय तत् पुनः । खम् उत्पेतुः सनगरा मायाम् आस्थाय दानवीम् ॥ ) 3. 170. 21; Arjuna steadied the town along with the demons and when broken by his iron arrows it fell down on the ground 3. 170. 26-27; Mātali praised Arjuna for his feat of destroying Hiraṇyapura,—a feat which could not be accomplished even by gods and Asuras 3. 170. 51-54; when the town was destroyed and the demons were killed (विध्वस्ते ऽथ पुरे तस्मिन् दानवेषु हतेषु च) the women of the demons came out of the town weeping aloud in grief 3. 170. 55-57; Arjuna, after destroying Hiraṇyapura and killing the Asuras (हिरण्यपुरम् आरुज्य निहत्य च महासुरान्), returned to Indra with Mātali 3. 170. 60-61; hearing from Mātali in details the exploits of Arjuna, (हिरण्य-पुरघातं च मायानां च निवारणम्), Indra exclaimed ‘well done’ 3. 170. 63-64; this exploit of Arjuna is referred to: (i) by Bhīṣma, when he referred to the boon granted by Nara and Nārāyaṇa to Indra, while addressing Duryodhana (ताभ्यां च सहितः शक्रो विजिग्ये दैत्यदानवान् ॥ नर इन्द्रस्य संग्रामे हत्वा शत्रून् … । पौ-लोमान् कालखञ्जांश् च) 5. 48. 13-14 (in the earlier account in 3. 170 Indra is not mentioned as taking part in the battle); (ii) again by Bhīṣma while reminding Duryodhana about the exploits of Arjuna (दानवानां सहस्राणि हिरण्यपुरवासिनाम् । हतान्य् एकरथेनाजौ) 5. 166. 34 (this could also be a reference to Nivātakavacas of Hiraṇyapura1); (iii) by Arjuna while telling Uttara his earlier exploits (अहम् इन्द्रस्य वचनात् संग्रामे ऽभ्यहनं पुरा । पौलोमान् कालखञ्जांश् च) 4. 56. 9 (actually, according to the account in 3. 170, Indra had not asked Arjuna to kill Paulomas and Kālakhañjas (there called Kālakeyas); Arjuna did this on his own; Indra had asked him to destroy the Nivāta-kavacas of Hiraṇyapura1 (3. 165. 10-11) which is mentioned by Arjuna in 4. 56. 11); (iv) by Yudhiṣṭhira when, while lamenting over the death of Abhimanyu, he referred to the feats of Arjuna (हिरण्यपुरवासिनः  … पौलोमाः सगणा हताः) 7. 49. 17; (v) possibly by Duryodhana while reminding Droṇa of Arjuna's exploits (दानवानां सहस्राणि हिरण्यपुरवासिनाम् । विजिग्ये पुरुषव्याघ्रः) 7. 160. 19. E. Simile: When the demons were killed the town Hiraṇyapura became unfit to be seen like a pond with its elephants killed or like a forest the trees of which had gone dry (हतनागम् इव ह्रदम् । शुष्कवृक्षम् इवारण्यम् अदृ-श्यम् अभवत् पुरम् ॥ ) 3. 170. 59.
हंसकायन: Haṃsakāyana m. (pl.): Name of a people. Their excellent Kṣatriyas, with weapons in hands, brought wealth by hundreds to Yudhiṣṭhira for his Rājasūya (हंसका-यनाः । … श्रेयांसः शस्त्रपाणयः आहार्-षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 13, 16.
हंसपद: Haṃsapada m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the twelfth day of the war, Haṃsa-padas and many others, led by Kṛtavarman and Kṛpa, formed the ‘eyes’ (चक्षुषी) of the Suparṇavyūha of the Kauravas 7. 19. 4, 6-7 (to be identified with Haṃsamārga ? Cf. Editor's Critical note on the stanza: “If they are the same people as Haṃsamārga mentioned in 6. 10. 68, then the B S reading Haṃsapatha would be preferable” Cr. edn. Vol. 9, p. 1147;) [See the next entry].
हंसमार्ग: Haṃsamārga m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा  … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (ताम्रा हंसमार्गाश् च) 6. 10. 68; [See Haṃsapada above].
हरिवर्ष: Harivarṣa nt. (sg.): Name of a Varṣa. A. Location: Beyond Himavant and Śveta mountains and the Hāṭakadeśa and Gandharvanagara which were near the Mānasa lake 2. 24. 27; 2. 25. 1-5 (see section C. Epic events below); according to another reference, beyond the Bhāratavarṣa and only beyond the Haimavatavarṣa and the Hemakūṭa mountain (इदं तु भारतं वर्षं ततो हैमवतं परम् । हेमकूटात् परं चैव हरिवर्षं प्रचक्षते ॥ ) 6. 7. 6. B. Qualities of men and of the land: In the Varṣas beyond the Himavant moun-tain in the north there are holy Janapadas where beings of all kinds live (तत्र पुण्या जनपदास् … । वसन्ति तेषु सत्त्वानि नाना-जातीनि सर्वशः ॥ ) 6. 7. 5; according to Saṃjaya the qualities of men living in the four युगस् of the Bhāratavarṣa were bettered by those who lived in the Haima-vata Varṣa and more than that by those in the Harivarṣa (गुणोत्तरं हैमवतं हरिवर्षं ततः परम्) 6. 11. 14; the lands around Harivarṣa were known as Uttara-kurus and no battles ever took place on that land (उत्तराः कुरवो ह्य् एते नात्र युद्धं प्रवर्तते) 2. 25. 11; for other charac-teristics of the land see Epic event (No. 1) below. C. Epic events: (1) Arjuna in his expedition to the north (दिशं धनपतेर् इष्टाम् 2. 23. 9; 2. 24. 1) before the Rājasūya went from the Hāṭaka Deśa to Harivarṣa; he wished to conquer also that Varṣa but was told by the gatekeepers, having large bodies and great strength, that the city could not be conquered by him; he should return since the city could not be entered by men; if men did enter, they would certainly die (इदं पुरं यः प्रविशेद् ध्रुवं स न भवेन् नरः) 2. 25. 10; (Nī., Bom. Ed. 2. 28. 10: न भवेत् म्रियेतेत्य् अर्थः); moreover, if Arjuna entered it he would not be able to see anything (नेह द्रक्ष्यसि किंचन । न हि मानुषदेहेन शक्यम् अत्राभिवीक्षितुम्) 2. 25. 11-12; Arjuna agreed to return from Harivarṣa if the country could not be entered by men; they asked him if they could do something for him; Arjuna desired sovereignty for Yudhi-ṣṭhira and some tribute for him (पार्थिवत्-वं चिकीर्षामि धर्मराजस्य धीमतः ।  … यत्किंचित् करवन् नः प्रदीयताम्); after receiving from the gatekeepers tribute in the form of heavenly garments, heavenly ornaments and heavenly stripped-off hairy skins of antelopes Arjuna turned back (ततो दिव्यानि वस्त्रानि दिव्यान्य् आभरणानि च । मोकाजिनानि दिव्यानि तस्मै ते प्रददुः करम् ॥ ) 2. 25. 13-16 (Nī., Bom. Ed. 2. 28. 16 reads क्षौमाजिनानि in place of मोकाजिनानि and explains क्षुमातसीविशेषः  … तत्तन्तुनिर्मितानि क्षौमाणि अजिनानि च । ); (2) Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to describe to him the Harivarṣa in details (how long the people there lived, the fruits they received for their actions, auspicious or otherwise, their past, present and future (प्रमाणम् आयुषः सूत फलं चापि शुभा-शुभम् । अनागतम् अतिक्रान्तं वर्तमानं च संजय) 6. 11. 1-2; Saṃjaya then told to him the qualities of the people of the Bhāratavarṣa in the four Yugas and further told him that the qualities were found in a higher degree in the Harivarṣa 6. 11. 3-14 (see above section B.).
हाटक: Hāṭaka m. (sg., pl.): Name of a country and its people. A. Location: Called Deśa (हाटकं नाम देशम्) 2. 25. 1, 3, 5; it lay be-yond the Śveta mountain (श्वेतपर्वतं  … समतिक्रम्य) 2. 25. 1; near the lake Mānasa and the country protected by Gandharvas (सरो मानसम् आसाद्य हाट-कान् अभितः … गन्धर्वरक्षितं देशम्) 2. 25. 4-5. B. Inhabitants: It was the abode of Kiṃpuruṣas and was protected by Guhyakas (देशं किंपुरुषावासम्  … देशं गुह्यकरक्षितम्) 2. 25. 1, 3. C. Epic event: Arjuna in his expedition to the north (दिशं धनपतेर् इष्टाम् 2. 23. 9; 2. 24. 1) before the Rājasūya reach-ed Hāṭakadeśa and won over the people through conciliation (तांस् तु सान्त्वेन निर्जित्य) 2. 25. 3-4.
हारहूण: Hārahūṇa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Epic events: Nakula in his expedition to the west (प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम् 2. 29. 2, 11; 2. 23. 10) before the Rājasūya brought Hārahūṇas under control (वशे चक्रे) 2. 29. 11; Hārahūṇas brought for Yudhiṣṭhira tribute of different kinds but were stopped at the gate (द्वारि वारितान्; द्वारि तिष्थन्ति वारिताः) 2. 47. 19-20, 25; the tribute described in details in 2. 47. 21-25; it consisted of different kinds of asses (रासभान्), cloth and silk of different kinds, hides, weapons, drinks and perfumes (रसान् गन्धांश् च) and jewels; (however, Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 29 interprets रसान् as juicy fruits: रसान् रसवन्ति तर्बुजा-दीनि); Hārahūṇas mentioned by Kṛṣṇa among those whose kings attended the Rājasūya and acted as servants (मही पालान् … हारहूणाश् … यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 18, 21-22 [very likely they formed a section of Hūṇas; see Hūṇa].
हुण्ड: Huṇḍa m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the second day of the war, Huṇḍas were among those who, led by Yudhiṣṭhira, stood at the back of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39-40) of Pāṇḍavas (हुण्डैश् च  … पृष्ठम् आसीद् युधिष्ठिरः) 6. 46. 47.
हूण: Hūṇa m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: North of Āryāvarta; mentioned by Saṃjaya among the northern Mlecchas of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (उत्तरा चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … । … हूणाः पार-तकैः सह) 6. 10. 63-64; also see B. Past event. B. Past event: While going to Mithilā from mountain Meru (मेरुशृङ्गे 12. 310. 11-12; मेरुपृष्ठे 12. 311. 12), Śuka after arriving at Bhāratavarṣa crossed many countries inhabited by Cīnas and Hūṇas before arriving at Āryāvarta; from there he went to Mithilā in Videha (स देशान् विविधान् पश्यंश् चीनहूणनिषेवितान् । आर्यावर्तम् इमं देशम् आजगाम महा-मुनिः) 12. 312. 15, 12, 19 [See Hāra-hūṇa].
हृदिक: Hṛdika m. (pl.): Name of a people. Kṛtavarman designated as the great chariot-fighter of Hṛdikas (हृदिकानां महारथम्) 8. 18. 62 (Hṛdika, father of Kṛtavarman, perhaps also designated after the people's name).
हैमवत: Haimavata nt. (sg.): Name of a Varṣa. A. Location: It lay immediately to the north of Bhāratavarṣa (इदं तु भारतं वर्षं ततो हैमवतम् परम्) 6. 7. 6; (also see D. Past event). B. Charac-teristic: Haimavatavarṣa was superior to Bhāratavarṣa in qualities and Harivarṣa was superior to Haimavatavarṣa (गुणोत्तरं हैमवतं हरिवर्षं ततः परम्) 6. 11. 14; (for the qualities of the people see Bhāratavarṣa in the Addenda to this volume). C. Epic event: Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to describe to him the longevity of the people of Haimavata, the auspicious or bad effects of their action and their past, present and future (तथा हैम-वतस्य च । प्रमाणम् आयुषः सूत फलं चापि शुभाशुभम् ॥ अनागतम् अतिक्रान्तं वर्तमानं च संजय । ) 6. 11. 1-2. D. Past event: Śuka while going to Mithilā from mountain Meru crossed the Haima-vatavarṣa before reaching the Bhāratavarṣa (वर्षं हैमवतं तथा । क्रमेणैव व्यतिक्रम्य भारतं वर्षम् आसदत् ॥ ) 12. 312. 14.
हैरण्यक: Hairaṇyaka nt. (sg.): Name of a Varṣa. It lay to the north of the Śveta Varṣa and the Śṛṅgavat mountain (श्वेताद् धै-रण्यकं परम् । वर्षम् अत्रावतं नाम ततः शृङ्गवतः परम् ॥ ) 6. 7. 35.
हैहय: Haihaya m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Description: Having strong arms (बाहुशालिन्) 12. 49. 65; of unbounded prowess (अमितौजस्) 5. 153. 4; famous (प्रथितात्मन्) 3. 182. 5; eminent Kṣatriyas (क्षत्रियर्षभ) 5. 153. 5; (क्षत्रिय-पुंगव) 12. 49. 66. B. Past events: (1) A certain prince, not named, of Haihayas thought that he had killed a sage mistaking him to be a deer; he reported the incident to Haihayas; dejected, Haihayas (दीन-मानसाः 3. 182. 7) went in search of the dead sage; they reached the hermitage of Tārkṣya Ariṣṭanemi; they were duly receiv-ed by him (तेषां पूजाम् अथाहरत् 3. 182. 9); Haihayas, however, considered that they were unworthy of the honour since they had killed a Brāhmaṇa; they told Ariṣṭanemi that they had searched for him but could not find him; then they were told by Ariṣṭanemi that they had commi-tted no sin since whom they thought they had killed was his son who was alive, and was present in his आश्रम; Haihayas asked Tārkṣya how his dead son came back to life; they were told that since Ariṣṭanemi and his son always acted truthfully and never cherished a lie, and since they follow-ed religion they had no fear from death (सत्यम् एवाभिजानीमो नानृते कुर्महे मनः । स्वधर्मम् अनुतिष्ठामस् तस्मान् मृत्युभयं न नः 3. 182. 17); when Haihayas knew that they were sinless, they were delighted (हृष्टाः) and they returned to their country 3. 182. 21; (2) Rāma Jāmadagnya killed thousands of Haihayas (हैहयसहस्राणि) along with Kārtavīrya Arjuna's sons and grandsons and made the earth full of their blood-stained mud (चकार भार्गव्ō राजन् महीं शोणित-कर्दमाम्) 12. 49. 45-46; after many years, the Earth when not properly protected by Kṣatriyas entered Rasātala and requested Kaśyapa to see that some eminent Kṣa-triyas protected her again; she specifically mentioned for this purpose the Kṣatriyas born in the family of Haihayas who were protected by her when Paraśurāma killed all Kṣatriyas (सन्ति … नृषु क्षत्रियपुंगवाः । हैहयानां कुले जातास् ते संरक्षन्तु मां मुने) 12. 49. 66; a reference to the killing of Haihayas and of Kārtavīrya is made in the Parvasaṃgrahaparvan while listing the events of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 117 (actually the event referred to here is des-cribed in the Śāntiparvan as noted above; the event briefly mentioned in the Āra-ṇyakaparvan is different; see the next); (3) King Sagara of Ikṣvāku family extirpated Haihayas and Tālajaṅghas (स हैहयान्-समुत्साद्य … ) 3. 104. 7; (4) Kṣatriya Haihayas were attacked by Brāhmaṇas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras; they were again and again defeated by the Haihayas; the Brāh-maṇas asked them the secret of their victory; Haihayas replied saying that on the battle-field they listened only to one among them who had superior judgement; the Brāh-maṇas and the rest who attacked them were divided, each following his own judgement; the Brāhmaṇas then chose one of them who was skilled in policies and defeated the Kṣatriya (Haihayas) (वयम् एकस्य शृणुमो महाबुद्धिमतो रणे । भवन्तस् तु पृथक् सर्वे स्वबुद्धिवशवर्तिनः ॥ ) 5. 153. 4-9; (5) Udāvarta, king of Haihayas, mentioned among the eighteen kings who, at the end of the युग (युगा-न्ते), extirpated their kinsmen, friends and relatives (ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञतीन् सुहृदश् च सबान्धवान् … हैहयानाम् उदावर्तो … युगान्ते … संभूताः) 5. 72. 11, 13, 17; these kings are described as disgraceful to their race and mean (कुलपांसनाः; कुलेषु पुरुषाधमाः). C. Certain kings referred to as one belonging to the Hai-haya people, one born in that line; or the kings of Haihayas; or foremost among the Haihayas: A.
